# F4 (part A): A global LightGBM model on the backtest, then freeze

*Generated by `python -m forecast.run_f4` from `results/f4_backtest.json`. Do not edit the numbers by
hand.*

## What this step does, in plain words

F3 showed how well simple rules forecast. F4 trains one machine-learning model (LightGBM, gradient-
boosted trees) for all series at once. It learns from the past: "an item that sold this much
recently, on this weekday, at this price, before this holiday, sold this much on day h". It is
checked on exactly the same {n_origins} backtest windows ({origins}), series and days as the F3
baselines, with the same error measures. The final holdout (from d_{first_holdout}) is not read,
scored or tuned on here. The chosen setup is frozen for one run on the holdout later (part B).

**Headline:** {headline}

## How the model is set up

- **One model, many series, direct horizons.** One row = (series, forecast origin, target day). The
  horizon h = 1..{horizon} is a feature, so one model forecasts all {horizon} days at once and never
  feeds its own forecasts back in.
- **Training rows.** For a backtest origin B, rows come from {tr_n} earlier origins, one every
  {tr_step} days, the newest at B − {tr_gap}. So every training target day is on or before B, and
  one year of history (every season and holiday once) is covered. That is {rows_range} rows per
  backtest origin.
- **Features as of the origin ({n_features} in total).** Recent means over 7/28/56/112 days, the
  same-weekday mean over 4 and 12 weeks, share of zero days, days since the last sale, listed days so
  far, ADI and CV², the last known price (F3's last-full-week rule, never a future price) and its
  ratio to the item's own one-year mean price, and item / department / store as categories.
  Calendar facts of the target day are known in advance: weekday, month, day of month, SNAP, event
  name and type, and the distance to the nearest event.
- **What it never sees.** No unit, price or listing after the origin. No price of the target day.
  Not even the price of the origin's own unfinished week. Tests change every value after an origin
  and check that no feature moves. A guard refuses any day from d_{first_holdout} on unless the
  one-shot holdout run asks for it explicitly.
- **Unlisted days** (not on sale) are never training targets and never scored. **{closed}** (stores
  closed) is dropped from the training targets, forecast as 0, and ignored in the history features.
- **Loss: Tweedie** (power {tweedie}). Daily sales are counts with many zeros and a long tail.
  Tweedie handles both and predicts the mean.

## 1. Tuning grid (backtest only)

## 7. Bias and weekly totals

The model's mean bias is {model_bias} units per series-day, and the slice total over all windows is
{model_slice_bias}% against the actual ({bb_short}: {bb_slice_bias}%). Weekly slice totals over the
{n_weeks} origin-weeks (forecast minus actual, as % of actual): {weekly_text}. For the first window
(origin d_{first_origin}, just after Christmas and New Year) the weekly errors are {first_week_model}
for the model and {first_week_bb} for {bb_short}. Per-week numbers are in `results/f4_backtest.json`.

the target day together: {cal_share}%. Gain shows what the trees split on, not cause and effect.

## 9. Memory and run time

The training table was estimated at {est_gb} GB per backtest origin before it was built (upper bound:
every series listed on every target day). It measured at most {meas_gb} GB (float32). Peak memory
of the whole run was {peak_gb} GB (as seen by Python's `resource` module).{mem_text} One fit took {fit_range} s. The grid took {grid_min} min and the
whole run {total_min} min on an 8-core, 8 GB Mac.

## 10. Frozen for the holdout (part B)

- `config/model_final.yaml` (written by this run): the chosen setting and number of trees, and the
  exact final recipe. Train on origins every {tr_step} days with targets up to d_{last_train}. Forecast
  from d_{last_train} for the holdout days. It also stores the sha256 of `config/model.yaml`, so the
  features cannot change unnoticed.
- `python -m forecast.run_f4_holdout` (not run yet) refuses to start if the git tree is not clean or
  `results/f4_holdout.json` already exists. It records the commit hash and scores the model and every
  F3 baseline on the holdout with these same metrics.
- For F5: forecasts, actuals and residuals (actual − forecast) per series, origin, horizon and method
  ({f5_rows} rows) are in `{f5_file}` (gitignored; per-item data is not redistributed).
